fact: The land is Ostmere (a Chequer name); folk just say 'the land' or 'here'.
The Chequer was a guild-empire of mages and clerks that ran for centuries on magic drawn cheaply from something vast under the land; its language stays bureaucratic to the end.
The thing under the land is the Deep Account to the Chequer and Old Warmth or the Sloom to folk; nobody with authority names it as more than warmth or an account.
The draw from the Deep Account grew dearer for generations because it was cooling, and nobody asked why something under the ground should cool like a body.

The Essart (~70 years before day 1) was deliberate, a budget decision: a long cold failed the Chequer's warm-farmed crops, the warm-farm account ran short, and the Chequer covered it by 'realising the principal', setting the source alight to release its warmth at once.
The burn was held in check by a ring of keels, each anchored by one living holder and paid for in the holder's memory; folk who have seen a keel call it a hearthstone.
The Essart worked for thirty years: warm ground, green winters, a little ash the Chequer called acceptable tithe.
The keels were linked to share load; at the Breaking (~40 years before day 1) one holder refused and let go, the snap-back jumped keel to keel, and most keels failed within days.
The Chequer fell inside one season of the Breaking; nobody had planned for a holder saying no, because every holder had put their own name forward.
Blame for the Breaking is honestly mixed: the Chequer built a machine that ran on nobodies, and one nobody's refusal was right and broke the world.
Folk date things 'before' and 'after the Breaking'.
The burn has run unheld for forty years; its tithe is the ash that never stops falling and rises as a veil over the sky.
Days run from brown twilight to grey and nights are black; only in the Clear does a pale sun show as a disc and cast real shadow.
Cracks in warm ground glow a dull red at night, so the Hollow glows faintly after dark.
Fire, candles and lamp-oil are precious.
The burn heats the ground from below along seams (cracks, warm rock, hot springs); away from seams the land is cold and dead and life clusters on seam lines like vent life.
The burn that broke the world is what keeps the survivors alive; putting it out would kill everything left.
Green crops (ashroot, a bitter barley, beans) grow only on warm ground, and well only in the Clear.
Weathered ash is fertile, so a field fallen under older ash is the best field, which is why Fields improve with time.
Fungus feeding on forty years of buried dead is the base of the food web; it fruits in the Drift.
Meat is scarce; fish in warm streams are pale and blind.
The Taking: a creature that keeps eating things that lived in the ash takes traits from what it ate, a little in a lifetime, a lot over generations, and fast in things that ate human dead.
Cooking through, washing in running water and fire spend the Taking's leftover, so cooked food is safe; folk say never eat a thing that ate a man.
People who ate wrong in the bad years carry small changes nobody mentions.
Streams run grey, warm springs on seams run clean, sand-and-charcoal filtering is a Crafting method, and cisterns fill in the Drift.
Small Chequer wards on old buildings still hold, anchored to keystones fed by seam warmth.
The Hollow is one of the few places with a surviving keel, and lives because the player held on; nobody knows this, the player included.
Old Warmth is folk faith, not a system: prayers to warm ground, a hand laid flat on a seam stone as a blessing, no singing in the Still, the Sloom not to be woken.
The faith is closer to the truth than it knows and wrong about what it means; it is never a currency, building bonus or mechanic.

The dry humor draws on the player's own yes, competence against status, Chequer bureaucracy surviving the apocalypse, the shrug, gallows humor never at a specific death's expense, and the journal's clinical understatement.
source: world.md#What the dry humor draws on

fact: Story content never crosses the Never list: no sexual violence, no harm to the young on screen, no animal cruelty on screen, no none-of-it-mattered twist, no karma meter, no second-run true ending, no notable betraying you.
Turns are spent only on five tropes (the amnesiac's past, fix the catastrophe, the running joke, the gentle stranger, the ending); every other trope resolves as promised.
source: world.md#Tropes: where the turns are spent

fact: Resolving as expected on purpose: the old mage is a real mentor, liches die by their anchor, the town pays for how it ends, the deep places are worse, the faithful are partly right, the first person who shows up stays.
source: world.md#Tropes: where the turns are spent

fact: What the player is told is only that they woke in a ruin, alone, with nothing, remembering nothing.

The player was an ordinary person bound as holder of the Hollow keel at the Essart, a volunteer: the registry's selection field reads, in effect, present, no dependants, and the tick beside 'offered self' is in the player's own hand.
The keel holds its holder too: the player does not age and comes back from death at the keel, the warm stone at the first camp.
Folk call those who return from death the kept and find it a known, odd thing, like a stammer; they do not know the kept are holders.
At each Black Drift the keel spends the holder's memory to hold on; the player forgets everything, the town that never knew why it lived falls apart, and the player wakes in its ruins.

This is the fourth time: four Black Drifts since the Breaking have each spent the player whole, and the ruins scavenged from day 1 are the player's own previous towns in layers; the one woken in is town 4's.
The player's memories were moved into the keel's hold, not destroyed, and some of what passes for luck in the Hollow is that.
The player is not irreplaceable: any person could hold a keel, the player is just the one who did and keeps saying yes.
Learning the truth lowers the player's status; it is not a loop and not predetermined: the previous towns were real and this run breaks the cycle.

What is under the land is implied only (cooling like a body, the breathing burn, the faith's taboo never thank the warmth, the even draw at B47); no game text names it, no sound comes from below, and there is no reveal, corpse-shaped land or map, or explaining character.
source: world.md#The thing under the land, implied

fact: Rule 1: nothing is made, only moved; a spell moves heat, light, motion, quick (growth), shape (binding), and at the deep end sense (memory, meaning).
Rule 2: every move pays a tithe as ash, rising with the difference in kind and with distance; mages' hands are grey to the wrist and a big working leaves a drift.
Rule 3: like calls like; a working is cheaper along a link (same material, a piece of the target, a name, shared history), and drops are reagents.
Cascades come from rule 3: a jump-shaped working runs along kin-links target to target.
Rule 4: a held working needs an anchor that carries its weight; stone holds small things fed by fuel, only a living mind holds great ones.
When an anchor lets go the moved thing snaps back with interest: why breaking a ward hurts, why breaking a lich's anchor kills it, why one keel failing pulled the next.
Rule 5: sense is the heaviest coin; a memory moves more than a forge-load of coal for almost no ash, which is why the Chequer paid in memory.
Where spent memory goes, nobody knows; mages know only that it works and roughly what it buys.
Spell grammar is what is moved, plus how it moves (a line, a spread, a jump, a hold), plus the link; Arcana teaches each piece and Spellcraft combines them.
The player relearns the rules in order 1 to 5, and magic solves a story problem only inside the rules the player has by then.
Magic's law of exchange is the Tally; mages keep tally, and its waste is called tithe or just ash.
The thing under the land does not balance in the Tally; mages call it an open account, and journal entries on it are never finished.
Wonder moves outward each region to the next thing not understood, and stops at the burn; by the end the player reads a keel like a ledger.
Magic is a tool, not the villain: people did what was done with it.
The burn breathes in a 21-real-day cycle of three 7-day seasons, the Still (days 1-7), the Drift (8-14) and the Clear (15-21); day 1 is the first day of the Still.
The Still: the burn holds its breath; no wind, ash hangs, fog in low ground, sound carries far; ambush predators and things from the ground; scouting slower and finds more; eerie lines weighted up.
The Drift: the exhale; warm wind, heavy ashfall, brown dark days, warm nights; roofs must be cleared, fungus blooms, ash is harvested, moths and the ash-bear hunt, fire-fed spells are cheaper.

The Clear: the inhale; cold wind toward the burn, the veil thins, a pale sun, frost and stars at night; crops grow fast, scribes can work, sight lines are long, light-moving spells are cheaper, frost threatens outposts.
Once every 9 to 12 years the exhale is enormous, a Black Drift, which strains every keel; Black Drifts are history and lore, never scheduled in play.
The last Black Drift was months before day 1.
Nobody can explain why a fire breathes.
A season adds and raises, never lowers; nothing is missable and nothing on the main path needs a season's content.
source: docs/decisions.md#Seasons change the game, more than slightly

fact: A typical 84-day run sees each season four times.
R1, the Hollow, opens day 1 (act days 1-21): a bowl valley on a warm seam with ash-grey scrub birch and thorn, a warm stream, old fields under ash and the ruins.
source: regions.md#R1, the Hollow (opens day 1; act days 1–21)

fact: The camp sits on the keel's capstone, a flat warm stone.
source: regions.md#R1, the Hollow (opens day 1; act days 1–21)

fact: R1's question is can you live (yes, slowly, then less slowly); its resources are scrap, flint, deadwood, ashroot, seam-warm clay, wolf pelts and meat, crow feathers, tallow.
source: regions.md#R1, the Hollow (opens day 1; act days 1–21)

fact: R1 threats ramp by days there: ashrats, lone wolves and crows (1-7); wolf packs, greycoats and the Drift ash-bear (8-14); greycoat packs, one seeded greycoat leader and light-tier bandits (15+).
source: regions.md#R1, the Hollow (opens day 1; act days 1–21)

fact: R1 has no outposts: the town grows in place, with projects P0 camp, P1 palisade, P2 hall, P3 ash road, and later P7 forge, P8 scriptorium and P14 hearth built there.
source: regions.md#R1, the Hollow (opens day 1; act days 1–21)

fact: R2, the Ashwood, opens day 20 (act days 22-35): a dead grey forest turned fungus forest, warm patches, half-buried Chequer road markers, a waystation on a hill.
source: regions.md#R2, the Ashwood (opens day 20; act days 22–35)

fact: R2's question is how big is the world and how odd are you; it yields charwood, resin, bracket fungus, ash-caps, spores, elk hide, moth-dust and road-iron.
source: regions.md#R2, the Ashwood (opens day 20; act days 22–35)

fact: R2 has the logging post outpost (P4), raided by mourners, and joint projects P5 waystation and P6 lift.
source: regions.md#R2, the Ashwood (opens day 20; act days 22–35)

fact: R3, the Seams, opens day 36 (act days 38-55): underground cracks, galleries, hot pools and glowing rock with Chequer works, warm, wet and lit red; the Warm live in a long gallery by a hot spring.
source: regions.md#R3, the Seams (opens day 36; act days 38–55)

fact: R3's question is what is the burn and what are you; it yields iron, copper, ruddle (a heat-holding red ore), glass sand, salts, sulphur, chitin, eel oil and Chequer glass.
source: regions.md#R3, the Seams (opens day 36; act days 38–55)

fact: R3 has the mining camp outpost (P9) by the Warm's spring with a trade line, and projects P7 forge, P8 scriptorium and P10 causeway.
source: regions.md#R3, the Seams (opens day 36; act days 38–55)

fact: R4, the Chequer seat, opens day 55 (act days 57-70): across drowned ash flats by causeway, a ruined Chequer city on a hill with the Tallyhouse (archive and registry), towers and dead fountains; some streets are warm because the Unpaid draw heat there.
source: regions.md#R4, the Chequer seat (opens day 55; act days 57–70)

fact: R4's question is why did it break; it yields records, Chequer tools and lenses, clockwork, fine glass, ward-stones, wasp paper and silver.
source: regions.md#R4, the Chequer seat (opens day 55; act days 57–70)

fact: R4 has the Tallyhouse watch outpost (P11) in a fortified gatehouse and the cold road project (P12), a line of held lamps out to R5.
source: regions.md#R4, the Chequer seat (opens day 55; act days 57–70)

fact: R5, Caldrigg, opens day 70 (act days 71-84): a frozen grey waste where heat was taken at the Essart, then rising warmth toward a red glow never reached; frost-grey scarps with lichen, dunes of old ash, and the refuser's keel.
R5's question is what is it and what can be done (unanswerable; something smaller); it yields cauk (a pale near-perfect anchor), live cinders, scarp lichen, stilled remains and frost-glass.

R5 has the last lamp outpost (P13); the final project P14, the Hearth, is built at home with inputs from every region; under E-d its act is the roll, the households' names entered at N8's table (B51).

Every region brings new land, resources and new methods for existing skills (never new skills), outpost sites, joint projects and one question it answers; threats ramp with time spent there, never with defences.
Each region has one linked-group creature as a cascade target: R1 wolf packs, R2 moth swarms, R3 crawler colonies, R4 wasp hives and lich-linked clerks, R5 strays.

The player's death returns them to the warm stone at camp; it costs no progress, levels or stores, comes only from a chosen fight or a story beat, gives progression once (B20), and each return adds one margin line of a small trivial forgetting.
Five regions make five acts of about 2.5 weeks each, and their questions run: how to survive, how big is the world, what is the burn and what am I, why did it break, what can be done.

B1 (day 1): the player wakes in a ruin under falling ash, alone, cold, remembering nothing; the opening runs on one-off actions (A1-A7): three pushes to stand, looking around (the cold, and Scavenging), the coat's book and charcoal stub, dead wood by hand, drying it, clearing a spot, ringing it with stones.

B2 (day 1, A8): a fire once the wood is dry; Crafting opens with a stool (rest recovers faster, open fire burns through its wood) and a fireback of stacked stone (fire burns longer, rest stays slow), each 3 dry wood from the fire's own fuel; the other is built later; the stool always wobbles.
B3 (weekly, day 2, P0): N1 walks out of the ash to the fire, alone and the last of five, sees food to spare and sits down; the town is founded from the camp.
B4 (day 3): N1's first offer, to fetch her people's cart from the ridge; the first you-said-yes line follows only a yes; the cart is gone with wolf prints round it (no, and).
B5 (day 4, foraging 5): the ground under the camp is warm, ash melts there first, and the cracks glow red at night.

B6 (day 5): the player's hand on the warm stone moves its heat into dying kindling unawares, leaving grey ash that won't wash off; Arcana opens as wonder; N1 sits on the far side of the fire that night.
B7 (day 6): wolves at the edge of the firelight that do not come in; combat opens with a plain fight that goes fine while the pack strips the drying racks.
B8 (day 8, clock): the first Drift; roofs to clear, the fungus bloom fills the larder for the first time, and crows that count.
B9 (day 9, 3 journal entries): the wolf entry opens with a margin note already in the player's own hand.
B10 (weekly, day 11, P1): the palisade closes; safety tier; the first families arrive broken.

B11 (day 12): the first guard takes the spear the player smithed; the first death in town is a light-tier stranger whose death was decided on arrival; by custom the town sits up with the body one night and burns it at first light, and with no name known his mark goes on the tally board without one; no physical effect, and the camp's stone is not used.

B12 (day 13): a cellar dug for stores holds none, only a Chequer tally-board scored with marks in groups, the last group unfinished, and a stool short on the same leg, which reads as a joke; no count matches anything.
B13 (day 15, clock): the first Clear; a pale sun and real shadows; the newcomers stop to look, the longest-settled keep working and don't look up; fields come alive.
B14 (day 16, P2): the hall and the first shared meal show everyone how far the stores won't go; belonging tier; N1 rises as notable and N2 rises with the hall.

B15 (day 18): warming a fire from a field stone fails, the stone goes cold and a fist of grey ash lies where the player's hand was, though the camp stone never has gone cold; rules 1 and 2 are learned; Spellcraft opens.

B16 (day 19): a newcomer stares through supper and is gone before dawn, bowl unwashed; next morning the near snares are found re-tied the player's way; a town-3 survivor whose hands kept what the rest lost, never named as one.
B17 (weekly, day 20, P3): the ash road clears at the cost of a light-tier road-cutter, the land past the first hill is grey as far as anyone sees, and R2 opens.

B18 (day 22): the Ashwood and its pilgrims, dead animals (an elk with shelf fungus along its spine) walked toward warm ground by fungus, drag-marks to every warm patch, played as pathos; no human corpse walks; the hunters bring in a walked elk and the meat is condemned.

B19 (day 23): N3 appears at the forest edge with no name and sleeves kept down; comes home, accepts what asks nothing back (food, a blanket, later the book) and declines anything that would keep or bind them (a place in a house, a hand, a rope to hold, a name); the town names them anyway; O-book is offered.

B20 (weekly, day 25, 3 R2 expeditions): the player dies on a chosen expedition and wakes at the warm stone; N1 says 'Kept, are you'; the next morning's job list has the player down for the worst job on the board, because they come back; the death mechanic exists from here.

B21 (day 27): N4 arrives, alone in looking strangely at the player about B20, decides it is a blessing; the faith's one taboo is never thank the warmth; N4 says the names of the dead at every burning and asks for the names nobody gave; N3 won't take a hand in N4's prayer ring.
B22 (day 29, P4): the first outpost; the player took the first supply run, mourners take the cart and learn the road; N5 rises reading their tracks.
B23 (day 31, arcana 25): rule 3 learned through a wolf-hair ward and the first cascade through a pack; mourners learn the hall's latch.

B24 (weekly, day 33, P5): the woken waystation's wall map shows the old network and a ring of marks round something in the far dark (the second of three circle showings: P6, B24, B49), one mark exactly where the camp is; N3 won't stay the night there.

B25 (day 35): the waystation's old ward opens to a Chequer seal, and the only one in town is on the player's wrist; N5 copies it on their own wrist in charcoal and the ward opens for them too, once; skill prestige opens around here.
B26 (weekly, day 36, P6): re-keying the Chequer lift opens R3 and spends the waystation's ward, which no longer opens for anyone.

B27 (day 38): vent-life and the Warm, who live by the seams, pray to them, and refuse trade with surface folk; they burn their dead, then read long lists of names off the lip of a hot crack, where generations of names are scratched into the rock, and say them into it; asked about anyone on the list they give the name and nothing else; N4 goes quiet.

B28 (day 39): keepers attack the companions and step round the player as a clerk steps round a crate with a docket on it, one scratching a mark on its slate each time; the expedition is driven out with a companion badly hurt.
B29 (day 41, P7): the forge brings esteem tier and N6, who looks at the player's wrist and says nothing; he offers N3 his hand, N3 doesn't take it, and he looks at them a while; N7 rises.

B30 (weekly, day 43, the midpoint): a keel chamber with a cot, a cup, a holder's mark matching the player's wrist, and by the cot tally marks like the cellar's; the player completes that they were bound to one.
B31 (day 45): N6 reluctantly teaches rules 4 and 5, giving the player's forgetting a mechanism.

B32 (day 46): a seam under the forge line surges and the player holds it shut with the shape N6 taught; over three days the logging post (P4) on the same seam goes cold, its stores freeze and a light-tier worker dies (cost: people); the goal turns from fix the world to keep this part of it.

B33 (day 48, P8): scribes, books and readable Chequer script; self-actualization tier; N8 rises and can read wrist seals, the player's naming the Hollow keel; N3 asks to be taught letters and copies the only ones they have off their own wrist, the name of a keel nobody in town knows.

B34 (weekly, day 50): N9 arrives and recognises the player's snare knot before the player, ties it back on the snare, says nothing, and works near the player from then on; the player has not aged; nobody names what she thinks.

B35 (day 51, P9): the Warm trade on condition their elder deals only with the player as one of the Hold's, at a steep price in goods; an old porter, asked whose he is, gives his late wife's name, and the elder scratches it on the crack's lip and says it into the crack; SB-face follows days later; then O-price.
B36 (day 53): N9's directions show the ruins are layers of towns with the player's hand on the walls and a stool in every layer; again lands; N4 says the words over the layers; no glyph.
B37 (day 55, P10): the causeway, run by N1, opens R4; N3 won't cross it.
B38 (day 57): the dead city, hollowed clerks, the Unpaid and wasp-nested records; a light-tier member of the expedition comes back hollowed.

B39 (day 59): the player finds N6's daybook first (R4, a wasp nest's edge, or his own pack): his signature beside a column of holders' names, and the costing with the struck remembrance line and his note; he sees it has been read, doesn't deny it, stays and teaches harder.

B40 (weekly, day 61): the registry, read with N8 and N9, holds the player's entry: selection field present, no dependants, and the tick beside 'offered self' in the player's own hand; N9 works out the binding date's arithmetic and says nothing; the yes joke becomes evidence; no mirror.
B41 (day 62): the keepers' standing orders in the Tallyhouse let a holder stand them down, so the keepers answer to the player.

B42 (weekly, day 64): the record of the Breaking, read with N8, shows the first failed keel and the cascade keel to keel; that keel's name is the one N3 copied at B33; never stated, only laid side by side.
B43 (day 66): N3 at the fire, and O-tell (tell them) is offered; either answer is a real story and neither costs progress.

B44 (day 68): N6 proposes the Chequer way, rebinding a holder (the player) for another generation; it works; asked for another way he says he has none, and nothing is laid out or pointed at; N9 speaks of the forgetting in town 1; N1 and N4 say nothing.
B45 (day 70, P12): N1 asks who will lead the lamp-setters hoping the player says no; the lamp road follows old cairns someone set before; a lamp-setter is lost to the cold; R5 opens.
B46 (day 71): the first push into the cold is turned back; the second finds rising heat toward the glow and things stilled mid-step.

B47 (weekly, day 73): at the turn of a breath every lamp on the road dims at once and everyone on the expedition goes cold by the same amount; the journal records the same loss beside each name and one unfinished line; nobody discusses it, N4 does not say the words.
B48 (day 74, P13): near the last lamp lies the refuser's keel, broken and cold, with N3's mark.

B49 (day 76): inside the refuser's keel, in Chequer oilcloth, the journal's torn front pages left by the you of town 4: town 3's design, a ring of small circles round a circle each ticked in pencil, the ticks crossed through, the first in its own stroke and the rest in one long one; no count, date or note in the player's hand; the names on a separate sheet under Chequer wax; O-pages is offered (turn: down).
B50 (day 78): the Hearth can be begun and O-final is offered with E-d, E-b and E-c where available, each cost stated plainly; no option costs nobody anything.

B51 (weekly, day 81, P14): per variant; under E-d the households queue at N8's table with the names of their dead and nothing else, and not every household comes; under E-b N6 rebinds the player; under E-c N3 lays a hand on the stone; the hold changes, and that night ash stops falling on the valley and comes down at the edge in a ring, the Rim.

B52 (day 82): per variant; under E-d N9 cannot call up her mother's face, and a name read aloud from the roll is one nobody in the room can place; most shrug, some don't; under E-b the town watches the player and N1 asks for nothing; under E-c N3 is at the stone the next morning.
B53 (day 84): the morning after, without fanfare; clean roofs swept anyway from habit; a lot of work to do; play continues.
The spine is 53 beats over days 1-84, one weekly beat every week and four beats a week from week 4 on; later reveals are bigger, never further apart.
Gates are mostly projects and skill levels, with two season-turn clock beats (B8, B13) that gate nothing; sharp routes land ~17% early, lazy ones ~17% late.
The front half reveals the world and the back half reveals the player; weekly beats in weeks 7-12 are each a reveal about the player.
source: spine.md#How the back half keeps the rate up

fact: Late on, R4 and R5 beats alternate with home beats (B43, B44, B50) so a slow expedition never stalls the spine.
source: spine.md#How the back half keeps the rate up

fact: Building falls F1-F5 (palisade, hall, granary, forge, watchtower) come only from the story on a maxed building, never from defence, and each is rebuilt better.
F1: in the Still, an out-of-place creature walks through the maxed palisade, which is rebuilt in stone.
F2: Drift ash-load brings the hall roof down at night while it is empty and everyone is at the fire; F3: mourners get the granary latch and knock over a lamp.
F4: the seam under the forge surges and cracks it; F5: a Clear-night frost-quake drops the watchtower, rebuilt with a Chequer lens.
Side beats (falls, season set pieces, outposts' stories, emergent social quests) keep the drip between spine beats; season set pieces are named but not yet written.
source: spine.md#How the back half keeps the rate up

fact: The ending is one informed choice (O-final) shaped by what was built; no karma meter, and the real ending is reachable on the first run on every route.

The possible fix (E-d) is remaking the Hollow keel as the Hearth, still anchored by the player, its upkeep paid from the town's remembrance of its dead, entered by name in N8's roll; nothing of the dead is used and the respawn stone is never involved.

The Hearth moves the falling ash out of the air over the valley to come down at the edge in a ring of grey dunes, the Rim, a visible border round the part of the world saved; beyond it the world still falls apart.

E-d, the roll: available with the scriptorium (B33) and self-actualization tier, no population gate; leave is given per name, a refusing household keeping its dead's faces; within days of entry nobody living can call up an entered person's face, and every later death is paid the same way; the Hearth banks the payments between Black Drifts and takes any shortfall from the player, some memory and not all; the design leans toward it but it is not the true ending; last image B53.

E-b, the Chequer way: the player alone, rebound by N6, always available from B44; it works for a generation and the player knows they will forget at the next Black Drift; last image: the player cuts the stool's leg short, with no line after it and no catchphrase.

E-c, the one who said no: N3 offers to hold, available only if O-book and O-tell were both accepted; their first binding yes; the player is released, starts to age and stops coming back from death; last image: N3's offer the next morning, not remembering they made it.
After any variant, play continues in the saved valley.
S-rim: which outposts are supplied at B51 decides whether the Rim includes them; the Hollow is the minimum; what you built is what you saved.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: S-notables gives one closing line per notable by arc state; S-factions reads emergent quest outcomes for the town's character.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: S-memory reads O-pages: read at B49 and copied into the chronicle, town 3's people survive as written names; sealed, nothing of them is left; nobody living remembers them, so entering them pays nothing.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: S-names reads the chronicle's recorded dead: under E-d the roll is the only memory of the dead there is and its length colours a line, showing the households that kept their dead out; under E-b and E-c it is a count; never a variant or penalty.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: S-yes picks one of three closing lines from the share of offers declined, stating facts and never judging.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: Ending offers O-book, O-tell, O-pages, O-price and O-final never move progress whether accepted or declined.
Fixed notables (N1, N3, N4, N6, N9) are the same person every save; risen notables (N2, N5, N7, N8, N10) are authored roles cast per save from whoever in town best fits when the gate opens.
All notables never die and never betray the player; they may be in danger and scrape through, and each rises from the light tier through something that happens, never by title.
N1 Lucy is the hard practical survivor, the voice of somebody has to; she arrives at B3 alone, the last of five lost before she came (never shown).
N1 wants the fire still lit tomorrow, and later for somebody else to say no for once; she brings most offers and most you-said-yes lines are her looking at the player.
N1's arc goes from survival to the town's conscience; after B40 she offers a job hoping the player declines and says nothing either way; epilogue: she runs the work and keeps asking.
N2 the cook (risen at B14, cast from whoever cooked most for others) keeps the hall's fire and pot, is the gossip and heart, is tested by a rations feud, and under E-d is first in the queue at B51.

N3 Sorrel is the sealed holder of the first keel who refused and let go, causing the Breaking; the load cascaded away, but the part of the working that holds its holder had nothing left to hold and keeps itself on N3's memory one day at a time, so they are unageing and remember only this morning.
source: cast.md#N3, Sorrel (fixed): the one who says no

fact: N3 is named by townsfolk from a seeded plant list (Sorrel by default); declines anything that would keep or bind them, gently and without knowing why; accepts what asks nothing back; keeps their sleeves down so their seal goes unseen until B33; no flinch.
source: cast.md#N3, Sorrel (fixed): the one who says no

fact: N3 wants to stop waking frightened; if O-book is accepted their pages become a daily diary that contradicts itself from day to day unnoticed; if told at O-tell they take it quietly, forget by morning, and the book remembers.
source: cast.md#N3, Sorrel (fixed): the one who says no

fact: N3 is never a villain: the refusal was right and broke the world anyway.
source: cast.md#N3, Sorrel (fixed): the one who says no

fact: N4 (role word bedesman, never faith-keeper) arrives at B21 walking seam to seam laying hands on warm stones, rises through the burnings, keeps the taboo never thank the warmth, and says the names of the dead at every burning.
N4 decides the player's return is a blessing; their faith is shaken by B32 and B47 and changes rather than breaks; under E-d they read the roll's new names at the Hearth; never a priest role bonus.
N5 the tracker (risen at B22 from the forager or hunter with most expeditions) scouts supply lines, loves the Ashwood, hates the Seams, and marks the Rim's edge at B51.
N6 Thompson is a stronger mage than the player throughout and never the hero; he arrives at B29, looks sixty and is past ninety.

N6 was a Chequer tallier who signed holders' papers, the player's among them; he survived the Breaking by moving his years into a ledger he carries, a held working paid in his own memories, a little of what the Unpaid became, stopped short.

N6 wants to be useful before he forgets why he is sorry; his daybook's costing priced the keels' upkeep from remembrance of the deceased and struck it, his note beside it reading requires the leave of every household, not obtainable (his wrong premise: leave can be given per name); he proposes the Chequer way because it works and his note says there is no other; under E-b he rebinds the player.
N7 the smith (risen at B29 from metalwork history or the most-used crafter) is competitive then fond, and never manages to fix the stool, which bothers them all game.

N8 the scribe (risen at B33 from a sharp, curious light-tier arrival) keeps the chronicle, reads Chequer script and wrist seals, reads the registry with the player at B40, and under E-d keeps the roll at whose table the climax happens.
N9 Margaret lived at eight in town 1, the player's first town after the Breaking, and was taught snares by the player; she is in her late forties and walks with a stick.
source: cast.md#N9, Margaret (fixed): the girl you looked after

fact: N9 arrives at B34 seeking a hall and people, knows the snare knot before the player and says nothing, directs B36's dig, does B40's arithmetic in silence, and under E-d loses her mother's face at B52; epilogue: she teaches a child to set snares.
source: cast.md#N9, Margaret (fixed): the girl you looked after

fact: N10 the cellar boss is risen emergently as leader of a clique that hardens into a gang; an emergent quest breaks it up, absorbs it into the guard or lets it grow; N10 may betray light-tier townsfolk but never the player.

Arrivals by tier: survival draws the lone and desperate; safety draws families always missing someone; belonging draws widowers, musicians, people walking toward any light; esteem draws masons and a form-loving Chequer clerk; self-actualization draws scholars and the curious.
Groups arrive broken with deaths decided on arrival; losses of the young are only past or off screen, at a rate set in code (young_loss_rate), never a frequency word.

Factions the social system can grow: the Hall (community; resists E-d, its households keeping their dead out of the roll), the Wall (guards), the Cellar (N10's gang), the Ledger (order; favours E-d as a costing), the Warm (external, R3), the Faithful (N4; divided on E-d).
source: cast.md#Factions and cliques the social system can grow

fact: The Wall splits on whether to send the kept one on every bad job, from B20's job board, and after B51 carries the dead home from outposts to be burned and entered; the Ledger's preference is never a notable's betrayal.
source: cast.md#Factions and cliques the social system can grow

fact: The Warm are seam folk who survived by the heat and pray to it; some raid, they trade, a few join the town; they are never monsters.
The player is just a person in way over their head: chosen by circumstance, never destiny; competence grows, status does not; the joke is only ever about choices the player made.
source: docs/decisions.md#Tone: gritty survival, dark story, dry humor

fact: Each region asks a different question of the survivor by kind: R1 hunger, R2 stealth and silence, R3 heat and machines, R4 the hollowed and the Unpaid, R5 cold and the unknowable.
Every creature is marked evolved, taken (bent by the Taking) or made; ordinary animals are hunted and fought plainly, taken and made ones are monsters.
Seam life runs on heat and minerals like vent life, with no sun.
Ashrats burrow in warm ground, breed all year, raid stores and come indoors in the Drift; they are base prey for everything.
Ash-deer are few, shy, the good meat, and rut in the Clear; their scarcity is why wolves turned to the dead.
Wolves are ordinary, in packs of 4-7, told plainly as a way of life.

Greycoats are wolves whose line ate the dead; they wait at the edge of the light facing it as if expecting to be asked in, have long forefoot toes, understand wards and fire, and have one seeded leader per save.
Tallymen are crows that ate the Chequer's battlefield dead and count under their breath in Chequer numbers; the count drops by one before anyone is told of a light-tier death.
The ash-bear is a plain Drift-only R1 threat with reversed seasons, denning in the Clear.
The ledger-hound is a Chequer construct with a seam-fed keystone heart, made to track holders who ran; a rare R1 wanderer from R3 that sits at the player's feet and fights whoever is beside them.
R2: bracket-elk carry fungus-shelf antlers and are dangerous in the Clear rut; hush-moths are Drift swarms whose dust deadens sound; ash-boar armour themselves in resin.
Mourners are lynx whose line ate the dead and took hands; they open latches and raid stores and supply lines.

Pilgrims are dead animals (elk, boar) the fungus walks slowly toward warm ground to fruit, leaving drag-marks; never a human; not hostile but their spores are, and walked meat is condemned; they show where seams are and are burned with N4's words.
The howlet is a man-tall owl, R2's apex, hunting silently in the Still.
Strays are loose workings left when keels failed, flames with no fuel moving heat at random, all linked to the burn; caught in lamps they become live cinders.
R3: crawlers are blind cat-sized woodlice in colonies that swarm toward light; glass-eels are transparent and yield clean lamp oil; kiln-salamanders draw heat by instinct with a cold-moving bite.
The seam-worm, R3's apex, burrows through hot rock by moving its heat ahead; its cold spots crack the forge (F4).

Keepers are Chequer constructs maintaining keels on seam heat, still on duty; they attack anyone near a keel who is not a holder and file a holder, stepping round them and scratching a mark on a slate; their orders are readable later in R4 records.
R4: paper wasps nest in archive paper full of record fragments; city cats are feral and harmless, and townsfolk adopt one as a companion that never dies.
Hollowed clerks are survivors the Unpaid fed on until only their jobs remain; lich-linked in groups so breaking a lich's anchor drops a street; some can be walked home, and they never recover.

The Unpaid are Chequer mages who moved their deaths into anchors (tally-sticks, ledgers) and feed on sense; finite, each named in the registry, outclassing the player until the anchor is found and broken; the oldest one's anchor ledger is the only list of those moved out before the Essart, and killing it burns the ledger (B38).
R5: tahr are the only meat; ounces are pale apex ambushers under the scarps that took their coat and stillness from the stilled things their line ate.
The stilled are things whose heat was taken at the instant of the Essart, not alive and not quite dead, some turning their heads in the Clear; environment, never explained.
Leaners are figures twice a man's height leaning toward the glow; approached, they turn their faces away; they never fight back, they leave; never explained.
The dune thing is a moving dune seen at night at most twice per save by an expedition, never fought, its sketch page blank but for one line.
One rare out-of-place creature per region, drawn at a code-set rate (rare_threat_rate) and bounded to a few per save, comes from a deeper region and previews it as a story moment, not a farm.
Clues are short and hooked, mostly mundane observations that turn ominous in hindsight, leave the last step to the reader, and live in journal, item lore, chronicle, beats or chatter.

fact: Unanswered on purpose: what the Deep Account is, what the even draw was, where spent memory goes, whether the reserve covers the next Black Drift, the Leaners, the dune thing, why the stool's leg is always short, why N3 said no, what lies past the glow and whether other keels hold elsewhere.
The Chequer map shows several keel marks not crossed out, an expansion hook.

At most one ominous line per journal page; crossed-out guesses get corrected as the player learns; rare old-ink notes (old_hand_rate) are already present, come from the selves of towns 2 to 4, may contradict each other and are not always right; the later pages carry a few small pencil notes near the gutter.

fact: The stool is one of the first two recipes on day 1 (with a fireback, each a visible tradeoff) and always wobbles, one leg short; no upgrade ever fixes it, only its material name changes.

The stool's beats: townsfolk fail to fix it in chatter, a matching stool in the cellar in week 2 reads as a joke, one per ruin layer in week 8 lands as again; E-b's last image is the leg being cut short, and other variants leave the stool where it stands.
Stool rules: never named as a motif, never explained, never more than one stool line in a day's unwrap, never in a dark moment's own line.

The yes: every job is an offer the player picks and declining costs nothing; lines land only after the player's yes, and at B40 the tick beside 'offered self' in the player's own hand turns the joke into evidence.

Day 1 opens on one-off narrative actions A1-A10, each run once (some in a few short pushes) with a log line that opens the next; the opening is 15-30 minutes of near-constant interaction, bars of seconds, up to the first leave-it-running moment.
Tools before skills: wood is gathered by hand until a flint edge is knapped (A9), which opens Woodcutting.

Fire needs dry wood: hand-gathered wood is damp from the Still's fog; drying (A5) runs while the player finds flint, clears a spot and rings it with stones; struck damp it never lights and dry it always does; Strike is offered before the wood is dry.
A cold status appears on looking around (A2) and clears when the fire is lit; the fire's falling fuel line is where standing orders first appear.
The player's coat holds the book and a stub of charcoal wrapped in a rag to write with; writing is never a mechanic.
Who is out there: the light on the ridge at the opening's dusk (opened by H1, advanced on every day-one visit, paid at B3 when N1 walks in).

Day one runs on the story's clock: the opening ends at story dusk on day 1, the night lasts about one game hour, and story day 2 lasts until B3 however long that takes; it is still the Still (no wind, fog in low ground, sound carries).

H1 (the first night): the ridge light is still there, kept low, and never moves; far off, one long howl carried by the still air; nothing comes near the camp. A11 (optional, sitting up with the fire): the light is minded the way you mind yours.
H2: a grey morning, the ridge light out; what the night got done is the unwrap.

H3 (A12, looking out past the gap): the Hollow by day, a bowl valley with fog in its bottom and the warm stream's steam rising out of it, old fields under ash and scrub birch; on the ridge where the light was, something dark and square that the dusk hid (N1's cart, B4), never named on day one.

H4 (A13, the first snare, with wire from the ruins): in the run the player chose an old snare is already set, decades old and rusted through, in the same place; nothing says whose it was or how it was tied.

H5: the camp's next two builds come as one choice, a lean-to (rest under cover) and a larder (food keeps); both get built and the order is the choice; the lean-to's open side faces the gap and the ridge.

H6: the snares catch ashrats and the smoking rack spends what is in the meat; at its first batch the smoke stands straight up in the still air all afternoon, visible for miles, so anyone can see the camp has meat.

H7: about an hour and a half after the first smoke, one set of prints comes through the gap to the larder; three roots are gone and a strip of smoked meat the player did not smoke is left on the warm stone; it is the same whether the player was watching or away (in-world the player was at the snares); it is N1, come to look, unnamed until B3.
B3 on day one: N1 walks out of the ash at the gap while the player takes stock (P0.4), eats from the larder, and sits at the fire on the player's side; the far side of the fire is B6's.
The smoking rack built on day one is among the drying racks the pack strips at B7, and the day-one snares are the first thread N9 pays at B34.

A14 (after setting the first snare, looking over the camp by daylight): ash has settled overnight on everything left out, the player included, and the roots stacked by the warm wall have gone soft; this is what brings the lean-to and the larder into view (H5). Nothing new about the ground under the camp.

The keels' costing priced their upkeep line by line; a line drawing it from remembrance of the deceased was struck, rejected, supply irregular, with N6's note beside it, requires the leave of every household, not obtainable; the upkeep went to the holders' own memory instead.

Chronology before day 1: ~70 years the Essart; 70-40 the thirty good years; ~40 the Breaking; 40-~30 town 1 (N9 a child); ~30-20 town 2 (that self died on the road out and woke at the stone); ~20-10 town 3 (a shared keel of about thirty unsealed people, who all forgot at once and scattered); ~10 years to months town 4 (found town 3's pages, sealed them at the refuser's keel; its ruin is where the player wakes).

A draw on the living cascades: a working drawing sense from one living mind runs along shared-history links to everyone that mind shares a life with, so a keel shared among the living is the Breaking in small and more sharers make it worse.

The Chequer seal on a holder's wrist shuts that mind's links to a working's draw, so a draw on a sealed holder goes no further; that is why holders were picked present, no dependants, and why every Black Drift stopped at the player.

A draw on a memory of the burned dead stops: fire spends what sense a body carries (the Taking), so the draw takes every living mind's memory of that person (face, voice, what they were like) and goes no further; an unburned body would let it through.

A written name is the address a draw finds its memory by, and the draw leaves it, since writing is not sense in a mind; the Warm scratch their dead's names on a crack's lip and keep the names while losing the rest.
The faith's custom: the dead are sat up with by the fire one night and burned at first light, the names of the dead are said at every burning, and the one taboo is never thank the warmth.
S-seam reads O-price (B35): if the town let the Warm go on saying its traders' dead into the seam, the cost was known in town before O-final, and the epilogue says so in one line.
source: spine.md#Strands (vary the epilogue under any variant)

fact: What no variant does: the burn still burns, the world past the Rim still falls apart, other keels still each have a holder forgetting at every Black Drift, N3 still forgets each day unless E-c, and the Unpaid still hold R4.

What can pay instead: the remembrance of the dead (opens B27; advanced B35, B39, B44; paid B50, shown, and B51, done; planted without fields by B11, B21 and SB-face).

fact: What is up on the ridge: the dark square H3 showed and never named (opened by J1, when N1 looks at the ridge after giving her name; advanced by J2 and the cart offer; paid by B4: her people's cart, and it is gone).

Day two runs on the story's clock from B3 to B4: the grey afternoon runs on until a quarter of a game hour after A15 (giving N1 the stool), then dusk, a second night of about one game hour, and story day 3, which lasts until B4; still the Still.
J1 (A15): the player gives N1 the stool; it rocks under her and she wedges the short leg with a chip of stone without remarking on it; she gives her name, Lucy, and looks at the ridge a long time.

J2 (the second night): with the two at the fire, a sound carries down from the ridge in the still air, wood dragged on stone, a long scrape, then nothing; N1 hears it and says nothing; from then the ridge's dark square is gone, which no line says.
J3 (morning of day 3): N1 is up before the player and has fed the fire; the stool's wedge is out and it rocks again.
J4 (A16, making room for two): N1 slept by the fire in the open; two builds come as one choice, a shelter for her and a woodstack; both get built and the order is the choice.

The cart offer (B4's ask): once her shelter is built N1 means to stay and asks the player to fetch her people's cart from the ridge; the player goes, or she goes herself, the same walk either way; whoever walks finds the cart gone, dragged off, wolf prints all round, and brings back only the news; if the player went, she takes it without a word.
From B3 N1 works for the camp: gathering work at a plain pace (she has no levels), foraging first because roots are what she lacked; she has her own knife; she does not tire or get cold in play.
Day three's near question, why the camp is not like the rest of the Hollow: opened by K1, advanced by K2, K3, K4 and K5, paid by B5.

K1 (A22, walking the edge): the camp sits in plain view of the ridge with scrub on three sides and one way out over the old fields, a half-sunk track; the ash lies thinner on the camp's stone than anywhere on the walk.
K2 (the track's first run): a stream along the track steams a little in the cold, ash does not lie on the water, and its bank is soft grey clay, warm in the hand.

K3 (night 3): howls answer each other across the Hollow, nearer than the first night's; Lucy banks the fire higher and says nothing; nothing comes; by morning frost greys everything past the firelight and none lies on the stone.
K4 (the track's second find): the track reaches the old field, furrows under the ash with nothing growing or able to; a ploughshare rusted to a lump in the last furrow comes back as scrap.

O-stay: a man drawn by the stew's smell waits at the firelight's edge, alone, carrying a spear's shaft with no head, and asks to stay; either answer gives him a place, the answer is whose hands build it.
K5 (the second arrival joins): he takes his place at the fire and gives his name, and Lucy looks him over once and goes back to work; light tier, named per save from the names pool.
B5 lands in night 4 when the player banks the new clay hearth on the camp stone for the first time; the cracks round the hearth glow faintly red.
